review_notes: I reviewed the whole file: FlatHistoryCuts, FlatLimitConditionCode and the lemmas about them. Both definitions are specific to the forcing development. FlatHistoryCuts says that for every stage beta, the history entry Q at beta contains pair row (assignmentCut levels beta A). FlatLimitConditionCode wraps this as a pair-coded predicate. I found no Mathlib, Batteries or core concept that these duplicate. They build on existing notions: ZFSet.pair and ZFSet.pair_injective from Mathlib, and FunctionGraphOn, which is defined in NatUnionCodes.lean as ∃ B, ZFSet.IsFunc A B f and so reuses Mathlib's IsFunc. I checked Mathlib's ZFC files for IsFunc and funs and found no restriction-of-graph or similar concept that graphRestriction or assignmentCut would compete with. Those two are defined outside this file in any case. The lemmas in this file are theorem-level results, which the rubric excludes. Residual uncertainty: I did not search the whole repo for a sibling copy of FlatHistoryCuts, and I did not examine the definitions of graphRestriction or assignmentCut beyond reading them.
